rows.why_long: PrizePicks higher 2.0 needs 57% per pick for your entry; fair view 38% (fanduel 1.5, moved to this line). Averaging 1.7 over the last 8 games, higher than 2.0 in 21% of them (raw 37%, shrunk 38%). Projects 1.9 (raw 40%, shrunk 38%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 2.0 on PrizePicks. Each pick has to win 57% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 1.5, moved to this line) is 38%.
Game log, most recent first: 1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 1, 0, 5. Weighted average 1.7; went higher than 2.0 in 2 of 8 games (21% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 2.0 vs 1.6 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.2, so the line is 0.3 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -4% on his average.
PFF: SF plays man on 20% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 24%); he gains 1.11 yds/route vs man and 1.40 vs zone → +1% from scheme.
PFF: SF allows 1.48 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.59) → -8% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 33% of his routes from the slot (1.27 yds/route there, 1.19 outside); SF allows 1.49 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.49 outside (league 1.46 / 1.67, opponent-adjusted) → -7% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 1.9 catches on average; in a typical game 1.3 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.7 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 37% and the matchup 40%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 38%, matchup 38%.
Bottom line: we give it 38% to win and it needs 57%. The edge is the difference: -18.5 points; that works out to about -32¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
